review_candidates.description: Kenya Transitions Manager (Professional Pathways Pillar) Organization Refugee Studies Centre Posted 7 Sep 2026 Closing date 21 Sep 2026 Job title: Transitions Manager (Professional Pathways Pillar) Location: RLRH office at the British Institute in Eastern Africa in Kileleshwa, Nairobi (with occasional travel) Salary: KSh 2,800,000 – 3,234,111 gross yearly + benefits. Hours: Full-time (37.5 hours per week) Contract type: Fixed-term 12-month contract. We expect to renew this contract; funding is secured until at least October 2028. Reporting to: Senior Programme Manager, Professional Pathways Pillar Closing Date: 21 September 2026, midday (EAT) Start Date: 19 October 2026 (desired) but flexible About The Refugee-Led Research Hub The Refugee-Led Research Hub (RLRH) supports individuals with lived experience of displacement to become leaders in fields related to human rights, forced migration, humanitarian response and development, politics, and law, among other areas. We do so by delivering academic and professional development programming to a global cohort of students who have been affected by displacement—as refugees, asylum seekers, IDPs, stateless, and beyond—supporting access to graduate degrees and advanced career opportunities. RLRH also creates opportunities for researchers with displacement backgrounds to lead primary and secondary research studies, from start to finish. RLRH’s team is comprised of colleagues who are deeply committed to advancing refugee leadership, the majority of whom have lived experience of displacement. Our network of staff, researchers, students, and other affiliates is made up of 1,400+ individuals across 80+ countries. RLRH has six active offices: our first was established in Nairobi in 2020, we have had an office at the University of Oxford since 2021, and we have since developed physical hubs in Kakuma refugee camp (Kenya), Kuala Lumpur (Malaysia), Kampala (Uganda), and in the Oxfordshire community (UK). From October 2025 RLRH is funded to serve as a technical partner for the Mastercard Foundations Scholars Program network, advancing an ambitious global agenda to support displacement-affected learners to access 1,000+ graduate-level scholarships at partner universities around the world. RLRH provides expert guidance and implements specialised programmes to help these learners enter university, thrive on course, and pursue meaningful and enduring careers on completion of their degrees. A complementary, refugee-led research agenda designed by RLRH colleagues produces insights to help Scholars Program partner universities and other stakeholders accelerate positive, long-lasting systems change. The Role Overview Of The Professional Pathways Pillar The Professional Pathways Pillar (PPP) supports individuals with displacement backgrounds to access career opportunities. We work most closely with RLRH affiliates who have completed our academic and research programmes and other students who have completed or are pursuing postgraduate degrees at partner universities. We also collaborate closely with allied organisations and universities to systematically strengthen the inclusion of refugees in the workforce. RLRH’s people-centred career advancement programming brings to life our vision of creating transformative refugee leadership in impactful professional settings throughout the world. We deliver three main interventions: Foundationally, we provide individualised career counselling to RLRH affiliates at any stage in their journey, helping them to identify career pathways that are well suited to their personal and professional skills, experiences, and aspirations. To build out core professional skills, we run a stipended six-month, in-person advanced traineeship for degree completers, which combines foundational professional training with deep mentorship. This is currently run in three of RLRH’s offices – in Kampala, Kakuma, and Nairobi, with plans for future expansion – in collaboration with our Research Pillar. To develop meaningful and sustained pathways, we facilitate paid external professional placements with values-aligned partnered employers who are active and influential across various sectors of interest to RLRH affiliates. Placements provide a supportive environment for affiliates to establish themselves in the workforce, building skills and profiles that will serve them for years to come. On top of our existing global footprint, the PPP will grow in the coming years in collaboration with the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program, with the aim of supporting African graduates across 20+ universities worldwide to transition to meaningful employment soon after completion of their degrees. By 2028, the programme expects to have enrolled 110 African displacement-affected graduates in the traineeship across RLRH’s physical hubs and facilitate 130 professional placements with employer partners. Overview Of Position The Transitions Manager is responsible for the design and delivery of the PPP’s professional development and employability support services for graduates affected by forced displacement. The postholder will develop and implement a portfolio of career readiness activities that prepare affiliates to successfully transition into placements, fellowships, employment opportunities, and other career pathways. Combining strategic programme development with direct affiliate support, this is a dynamic role involving the delivery of high-quality online and in-person career coaching, group workshops, and application support. Through these activities, the postholder will equip affiliates with the knowledge, skills, and confidence needed to navigate the barriers frequently faced by refugee and displaced professionals pursuing meaningful career opportunities. The postholder will draw on their expertise, alongside insights from RLRH affiliates and university and employer partners to inform the expansion and strengthening of the PPP’s professional development services. As this area of work grows, the Transitions Manager will play a vital role in supporting the development and management of a broader careers function, contributing to staff supervision and the professional development of junior colleagues. This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced careers or employability professional to build and lead a growing area of RLRH's transition to employment work. Working closely with Professional Pathways team members, they will help create innovative and impactful services that support refugee and displaced graduates to pursue and achieve their long-term career goals. Responsibilities Professional development services design and improvement (35%) Lead the design of professional development services for RLRH affiliates, piloting workshops, practical resources and application support sessions. Produce and maintain clear documentation outlining programme design and implementation. Use participant engagement, feedback, and emerging needs to inform the continuous improvement of professional development services. Keep abreast of labour market trends and placement opportunities to inform programme content and participant guidance. Participant support and delivery (35%) Deliver 1:1 career coaching to programme participants. Facilitate group-based workshops and employability sessions. Lead the onboarding and induction of participants into placements and other Professional Pathways Pillar programmes. Match affiliates to relevant opportunities and provide career readiness support. Collaborate with PPP colleagues and Research Facilitators to support Graduate Trainees and placement participants. Technical expertise and external guidance (15%) Work closely with the PPP’s Partnerships Manager to provide technical support to professional transitions leads at Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program universities and other allied institutions. Deliver transitions-related workshops with university partners to master’s graduates who have been affected by displacement. Supervise and support incoming RLRH Careers Advisors as the portfolio of professional development services expands. Operations and administration (10%) Maintain case management systems and participant records to track professional development progress and outcomes. Other duties as assigned (5%) Attend PPP team meetings and contribute to planning and coordination activities. Undertake additional responsibilities aligned with the role’s purpose and organisational priorities, as directed by the PPP’s Senior Programme Manager. Selection criteria Essential A bachelor’s degree in education, human resources, social sciences, international development or a related field, or equivalent professional experience in career development. Significant experience in careers guidance, employability, professional development, career coaching, talent development, or workforce transitions. Demonstrated experience designing and delivering employability, professional development or career readiness programmes. Demonstrated experience delivering workshops, group learning programmes and 1:1 career coaching. Experience working with refugees, displaced populations, or other individuals facing barriers to employment, education, or professional progression. Experience maintaining participant records and using CRM, database, or case management systems to support programme delivery Demonstrated knowledge of labour market trends, recruitment processes, and career pathways, particularly within the African context. Excellent interpersonal and relationship management skills, with experience working across diverse teams. Strong organisational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities independently. Commitment to inclusion, equity, and affiliate-centred practice and programming. Excellent cultural competency and cultural humility. Excellent written and verbal English. Desirable A master’s degree in a relevant field of studies. Experience working within nonprofit, higher education, and/or international development environments. Experience working across multiple regions, particularly in LMIC contexts. Fluency in additional languages spoken by RLRH learners and affiliates, such as French, Swahili, Arabic, Amharic, Somali, and/or Oromo. Demonstrated experience supervising, mentoring, or supporting the professional development of colleagues. Professional qualification in career guidance, coaching, counselling, learning and development or related fields. Applicants are expected to have or obtain the right to work in Kenya. For candidates affected by displacement who do not currently have this, RLRH can provide support for acquiring a gratis Refugee Class M work permit. We believe that lived experience of displacement is a strength, and we give active, positive consideration to those with intersecting identities and backgrounds as part of our commitment to equitable hiring practices. As such, RLRH encourages applications from individuals who have been affected by displacement and others who may belong to historically under-represented groups, including but not limited to those who identify as BIPOC, LGBTQI+, women, and differently-abled candidates. In line with RLRH’s AI use policy, we kindly ask that you do not use generative AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT) to draft or edit your application materials. We are committed to ensuring that everyone has an equal opportunity to apply and be considered for any role, and our recruitment process is accessible to all candidates. If you would like to request an adjustment (including requests for alternative formats) to our process, please contact our team at careers@refugeeledresearch.org How to apply How To Apply To apply, please complete the online application form. As part of the form, you will be asked to: Upload your CV in PDF format (maximum 2 pages) Upload a cover letter in PDF format that addresses your fit for the essential selection criteria. Please include, among other things, details about: Your experience developing and maintaining a range of partnerships to widen participation or increase access to opportunities. Your motivation for applying to work with the Refugee-Led Research Hub and how this contributes to your longer-term professional goals. What refugee leadership means to you and how you support it Provide details of two references (Name, email, organisation and relationship to the candidate) Complete a short set of Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) questions. Your answers to the following questions are entirely optional. This information will not be used as selection criteria. If you'd rather not share this information, feel free to select "Prefer not to say". review_candidates.description: Organizational Context The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191-member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability. IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe. The IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles. The IFRC is scaling up a national society‑led response centred on community engagement, surveillance, and infection control, supported by an emergency appeal. Red Cross volunteers are mobilized in affected areas to conduct door‑to‑door awareness, counter misinformation, encourage early care‑seeking, and support safe and dignified burials, key to breaking transmission. At the same time, the IFRC is coordinating closely with governments and partners, strengthening cross border preparedness, mobilizing resources and surge capacity, and supporting logistics, infection prevention control, and community-based surveillance to contain the outbreak and reduce regional spread. The Ebola outbreak, declared mid‑May 2026, is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, with hundreds of suspected cases and hundreds of deaths reported across Ituri, South Kivu and North Kivu provinces. It began with clusters of unexplained deaths in early May and is spreading in a context of weak health systems, population movement, insecurity, and community mistrust, which together increase the risk of sustained transmission and cross‑border spread to neighboring countries such as Uganda and South Sudan. The absence of an approved vaccine or specific treatment for this strain makes the outbreak particularly complex and heightens the urgency of rapid containment. The PMER Senior Officer is reporting to the Deputy Operations Manager in Kinshasa and integrates the team of the delegation. The technical manager of this position is the PMER Coordinator in the cluster delegation. S/he integrates the regional and global PMER and Quality Assurance teams Job Purpose The PMER Senior Officer is responsible for implementing a PMER framework for the operation and for strengthening the quality of PMER systems and functions, by providing technical assistance and guidance across all relevant areas of PMER – planning, monitoring, evaluation/review, reporting, learning, and accountability. Maintain good communications and liaise with technical/operational counterparts, particularly IM and CEA, and with NS staff and volunteers, to ensure that plans are informed by accurate and relevant information and by the voice of those affected. Monitoring Support the development and implementation of an M&E plan for the operation, including outlining data sources, collection methods (quantitative and qualitative), frequency, and audience. Provide technical guidance to programme staff to help them incorporate appropriate M&E systems (e.g. post-distribution monitoring (PDM)) for their areas of expertise, including setting up indicators. Assist with the development and implementation of monitoring tools and activities to capture and provide reliable and timely monitoring data to inform quality programming. Work closely with IM and CEA colleagues, if present, to ensure that planned monitoring is well informed by available information/data and engages with and reflects the voice of the affected population. Undertake field monitoring visits with technical and NS teams. Support or prepare analysis of monitoring through reports, data visualization, and ensure it is evidence-based, user-friendly, and accessible for those managing the operation to inform decision-making. Evaluation / Review Prepare, design, and implement any necessary surveys, such as baseline surveys, reviews, evaluations, lesson learning exercises, or other relevant studies in response to operational requirements of the BVD operations. Participate in any internal reviews of operational progress, including lesson learning reviews. Verify all review or evaluation work is evidence-based and considers outcomes as well as outputs of the response to inform future operational decision-making and quality programming. Job Duties And Responsibilities (continued) Reporting Coordinate all reporting activities closely with the PMER Coordinator in the cluster delegation with operational leadership and the Regional PMER team – including agreeing on a reporting timetable and deadlines.
